title: How to care for a rudraksha mala so it lasts
description: How to clean, oil, dry and store a rudraksha mala, with separate care steps for thread malas and for chain malas that have gold-plated pendants.
intro: A rudraksha mala lasts for years if you keep it dry, keep chemicals away from it, clean it gently every few weeks and store it in a soft pouch. The one thing to get right is knowing what your mala is made of, because a thread mala and a chain mala with a gold-plated pendant need slightly different care. Here is a practical routine for both.

sections.heading: First, know what you are caring for
paragraphs: Rudraksha beads are dried seeds. They are hard, but they are still natural material: they can dry out and crack, absorb oils and dirt into their grooves, and swell slightly if soaked. The thread holding them is the weakest part of a traditional mala and wears out over time.

A chain-style mala adds two more parts: the metal chain and the pendant. On pieces like the [rudraksha chain malas at Varaha](/divine), the pendants are gold-plated. Plating is a thin layer of colour over a base metal, and it is affected by water, sweat, perfume and rubbing. So a rule that suits the beads, like oiling, can be bad for the plating if you are careless. Keep both in mind as you read the steps below.

sections.heading: Everyday habits that make the biggest difference
paragraphs: Most damage happens slowly, from small daily exposures rather than one accident. These habits prevent most of it.
list: Put perfume, deodorant and body lotion on first, let them dry, then wear the mala.
Take it off before bathing, swimming, or a sweaty workout.
Keep hand sanitiser and cleaning liquids off the beads and chain.
Wipe the mala with a soft, dry cotton cloth when you take it off at night.
Do not leave it in direct sun on a car dashboard or windowsill; beads can dry out and plating can dull.

sections.heading: Cleaning the beads, step by step
paragraphs: Every three or four weeks, or whenever the grooves look dusty, give the beads a gentle clean. For a thread mala, take a soft toothbrush with dry bristles and brush along the grooves of each bead. If there is stubborn dirt, dip the brush in plain lukewarm water, shake off the excess and brush again. Do not use soap, detergent or shampoo; they leave residue inside the grooves.
Pat the beads with a towel, then let the mala dry fully in the shade before wearing or storing it. Never soak a mala for long periods, and never dry it with a hair dryer on high heat.

For a chain mala, clean only the beads with a barely damp brush, holding the pendant and chain away from the water. Wipe everything dry straight after. The metal parts need nothing more than a dry cloth.

sections.heading: Oiling: the traditional practice and a caution
paragraphs: Many families oil rudraksha beads once every month or two to keep them from drying out. Sandalwood oil, mustard oil or plain coconut oil are all used, depending on the region. Apply a few drops on a cotton bud, rub it into each bead, leave it for a few hours and wipe off the extra. Too much oil attracts dust, so less is better.

On a chain mala, keep oil well away from the pendant and chain. Oil can leave a film on plating and trap dirt against it, which dulls the finish. Oil each bead with a cotton bud only, or skip oiling entirely if your beads still look healthy.

sections.heading: Storing it between wears
paragraphs: A small cotton or silk pouch is ideal. Many people keep their mala in the home mandir or in a clean box nearby. If you also own other jewellery, store the mala separately so harder stones and metal pieces do not scratch the beads or the pendant.
For chain malas, a zip pouch with a little silica gel sachet helps in humid cities and during the monsoon. Lay the chain flat or loosely coiled so it does not knot.

sections.heading: Signs your mala needs attention
paragraphs: Check your mala every month or so. These are the common warning signs and what to do:
list: Thread looks fuzzy or thin near the guru bead: get it restrung before it snaps.
A bead has a hairline crack: keep it dry and avoid oiling that bead heavily; replace it if the crack widens.
Beads look pale and dusty even after brushing: a light oiling usually brings the colour back.
The pendant colour looks patchy: plating wears with time; wipe it dry more often and store it in a pouch.
The clasp feels loose: get it checked so you do not lose the mala on a busy day.

faq.q: Can I wash a rudraksha mala with soap?
faq.a: It is better not to. Soap residue stays in the grooves. Use a soft brush with plain water and dry the mala in the shade.

faq.q: How often should rudraksha be oiled?
faq.a: Many families oil it once every month or two. Use only a few drops and keep oil off any plated pendant or chain.

faq.q: Can I wear my rudraksha chain in the shower?
faq.a: It is best to remove it. Water, soap and shampoo wear down plating and can weaken thread and beads over time.
